methodology: Built entirely from primary-source research, not a downloadable dataset -- this is the 'DARK: we build it ourselves' case named in docs/WANTLIST.md item #1. For each candidate case, ran targeted web searches (Exa neural + keyword search across DOJ/USAO press releases, state Attorney General/Auditor releases, federal appellate case law via FindLaw/Justia/govinfo/casetext, and major-outlet reporting: AP, NPR, NYT-affiliated regional dailies, Reuters-syndicated wires, and named metro papers). Verified for EVERY case: (1) a named individual with a criminal CONVICTION -- guilty verdict at trial or guilty/no-contest/Alford plea, never a mere indictment or civil settlement; (2) 2+ independent citations, preferring one official source (DOJ/USAO press release, state AG/Auditor release, or court record) plus one major-outlet or wire story, with a few smaller-town cases relying on two independent journalistic/official sources where a DOJ release did not exist (state auditor press releases treated as 'official' tier for state-level cases); (3) the office/entity is municipal, county, school-district, or special-district in nature, explicitly excluding purely federal officials, state governors, and private-sector-only fraud; (4) a quantified dollar figure tied to the conviction record, court filing, or official audit -- not a bare allegation.
inclusion_rules_applied: Name individuals ONLY from conviction records (guilty verdict, guilty plea, no-contest plea, or Alford plea) and major-outlet/official reporting of that conviction. Zero entries in this ledger rest on allegation-only status.

Every entry carries 2+ citations. Where a DOJ/USAO or state AG/Auditor press release existed, it was used as the 'official' citation; a major-outlet or wire story (or, for smaller cases, two independent local/regional outlets) supplies the second.

Public officials and public corruption only. Excluded: private-sector-only fraud, federal officials (members of Congress, federal agency heads), and state governors -- per the task brief's explicit carve-out. The one exception permitted is ABSCAM's Camden mayor and a Philadelphia city councilman, kept because they ARE municipal officials caught in a sting that separately implicated federal officials; those federal co-defendants (1 senator, 6 representatives) are explicitly NOT counted or named as 'who' in this ledger's record, only referenced in the scheme narrative for context.

Verified amounts only. Where court-established and press-estimated figures diverged, the court-established figure (restitution order, forfeiture order, or trial-established loss amount) was used as the primary 'v' value, with the range or discrepancy noted in the record's outcome/scheme text where material (see Jefferson County/Langford entry for the clearest example: personal bribe take $241,843 vs. fees diverted to his benefactor $7.2M vs. the county's unrelated $3B+ sewer-debt/bankruptcy context -- all three numbers are named explicitly and NOT conflated).

Layer-specific amount convention: 'v' records the dollar figure most directly tied to the CONVICTED conduct and cited sourcing for that specific record -- for a few multi-defendant cases (Beaumont, Crystal City, Cuyahoga County, Maverick County) this is the scheme-wide total rather than a single defendant's personal take, since the conviction record establishes the scheme total and multiple named co-defendants share it; this is disclosed in each such record's 'who' and 'outcome' fields.

Mayor Barry Moore's sole conviction was for selling oxycodone, explicitly unrelated to the town's financial misconduct. The state audit's findings (31 violations, a clerk overpaid by $9,000, $27,000 spent without documented public purpose) are administrative audit findings, not criminal convictions with a quantified theft. The oft-repeated '$1 million in missing funds' figure is a characterization of the town's overall bookkeeping chaos, not a proven theft by any convicted person. Removed per protocol rule 2: 'Allegations without convictions are not data.' This corrects the original drafting pass's decision to keep this record at v=0 as a 'brief-named seed anchor' -- on reflection, being brief-named does not exempt a record from the core inclusion bar when no convicted individual has a quantified financial-crime amount.

amount_verification_notes: Dixon/Crundwell: press and court sources cite figures from '$53 million' to '$53.7 million' to a 7th Circuit opinion's 'approximately $53 million.' Used the court's own restitution order and the DOJ press release headline figure, $53.7M, as the canonical figure -- this is the number the sentencing court ordered her to repay.

Jefferson County/Langford: THREE distinct dollar figures exist in reporting and must never be conflated -- (a) $241,843, Langford's personal bribe take (cash, clothing, jewelry) per his forfeiture order; (b) ~$7.1-7.2M, the fees his bribery-driven steering generated for his benefactor Bill Blount's firm (this ledger's recorded v); (c) $3B+, Jefferson County's total sewer-system debt/bankruptcy exposure, which is a separate financing-crisis figure not identical to any individual's theft. All three are stated explicitly in the record.

Beaumont/Kapanicas et al.: press reports the SCHEME total as 'almost $43 million' (DA's charging figure, based on a 2014 civil judgment ordering the city to pay WRCOG $43M) vs. the CRIMINAL restitution actually ordered across all five pleading defendants, which totaled just over $11M (Kapanicas $1M + Aylward $100K + Dillon $4M + Egger $3M + Moorjani $3M). Recorded v=$43M as the court/DA-established scheme-scale figure (matching the civil judgment amount, which is itself court-established), with the smaller aggregate personal-restitution figure disclosed in the outcome text -- flagged as the clearest case in this ledger where 'scheme size' and 'restitution collected' diverge sharply.

Santa Cruz County/Gutfahr: DOJ/IRS sourcing states she embezzled 'approximately $38.7 million' and was ordered to pay $51.8M restitution (the larger figure includes interest/penalties/tax owed, not just principal stolen). Recorded v=$38.7M as the principal-theft figure per her guilty plea; the larger restitution figure is disclosed in the outcome text.

Panoche Water District/Falaschi: this is the ledger's one 'special district, water theft' entry. The $25M+ figure is BOR's valuation of 42 billion gallons of diverted water over 23 years -- a resource-theft valuation, not a cash-embezzlement figure -- disclosed explicitly as such in the record. Falaschi's actual criminal sentence (probation, home detention, $10K fine) is comparatively light because he pleaded to conspiracy/tax charges rather than a theft charge carrying a dollar-value sentencing enhancement; the district separately paid $8.26M in civil settlements to the federal government and a water authority, also disclosed.

Atlanta/Bickers: the $17M figure is the total value of contracts steered (sidewalk, bridge, snow-removal work), not Bickers' personal take; her personal bribe intake is reported at approximately $2M. Recorded v=$17M (the scheme's diverted-contract value, matching how DOJ/press describe the scale of the corruption) with the $2M personal-bribe figure disclosed in the outcome text.

Maverick County, TX and Crystal City, TX: both are multi-defendant scheme totals (prosecutors' 2-year cost estimate for Maverick; a specific $2.25M diverted debt-offering tranche for Crystal City) rather than any single defendant's personal enrichment -- disclosed in each record's who/outcome fields.

counts.smallest_dollar_entry: Crawford, NY (Jolene Roy) at $21,296 -- kept despite its small size specifically to represent the vast population of small-town clerk/treasurer embezzlement cases that make up the bulk of ACTUAL municipal corruption convictions in the U.S., in deliberate tension with the handful of eye-popping Crundwell/Beaumont-scale cases at the top.

caveats: This ledger is NOT exhaustive -- it is a curated 44-case selection (originally drafted at 46, reduced by 2 in a 2026-07-07 citation-completion QA pass; see citation_completion_pass above) built for a v0.5 acquisition slate targeting roughly 40 cases per the task brief, itself an early tranche toward the WANTLIST's eventual goal of 'curated ~100 cases.' Hundreds of additional convicted municipal-corruption cases exist; this pass prioritized (a) the task's named seed anchors, (b) cases with the largest verified dollar amounts, (c) cases with the most audacious/memorable schemes, and (d) deliberate era and regional spread once the largest cases were locked in.

Several records represent SCHEME-WIDE totals shared across multiple convicted co-defendants rather than one person's personal enrichment; this is disclosed per-record (see amount_verification_notes) rather than hidden, but a reader skimming only the 'v' field and 'who' field without reading 'outcome' could misread scale for an individual's personal theft. This is a known limitation of a single scalar 'v' field applied to multi-defendant conspiracies.

Coordinates are city/place-level centroids (from data/ref/us_places.csv where available, else Google Geocode for places too small for that reference file -- Vernon CA, Panoche CA, La Porte IN, and several county-seat/township lookups). These pin the STORY to a place, not a literal crime-scene location -- e.g., 'Hidalgo County, TX' is pinned near the county seat area though the underlying bribery targeted Weslaco city contracts specifically; the record name clarifies this in-text.

Sentences described reflect the sentence AS IMPOSED at the cited source's publication date; a small number of these individuals have since had sentences commuted (Kilpatrick, Nagin -- both received presidential clemency after the cited sentencing articles were published) or resentenced on appeal (Spaccia's Bell sentence was reduced from 11y8m to 10y after an appellate reversal of some counts). Both the original sentence and any known subsequent commutation/resentencing are noted in the relevant records' outcome text where discovered during research.

A handful of entries (Fairview Township PA/McGinnis, sentenced March 2026; and several other 2025-2026 cases) are extremely recent relative to the survey's 2026-07-07 retrieval date -- these were verified against IRS-CI and USAO press releases plus regional-paper follow-up coverage, the freshest sourcing tier available, but have not had years to accumulate the kind of secondary/retrospective coverage that anchors the older seed cases.

The task brief's suggestion to check 'Harvey/Dixmoor IL cases' surfaced two cases that, on close inspection, FAIL the binding protocol (Harvey's mayor has no conviction; Dixmoor's mayor's actual conviction is for a small, unrelated benefits-fraud charge) -- this is reported transparently rather than papered over with a weaker substitute, consistent with the survey's standing law of 'no fabricated records, gates named honestly.'
